source.title: Towards Measuring Representational Similarity of Large Language Models
source.authors: Max Klabunde; Mehdi Ben Amor; Michael Granitzer; Florian Lemmerich

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity across current-generation LLMs and reports that similarity varies by model, task, and metric, refining the idea of broad representational convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports heatmap comparisons and summarizes several model- and measure-specific patterns in the text. Individual heatmap cells are not numerically labeled in the supplied text; those values are not inferred. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures final-token, last-layer representational similarity across 11–13 independently trained ~7B base LLMs from different families, using several measures on two datasets. It reports that similarity is non-uniform and depends on the measure and the task. Those results bear on V6 (metric and data dependence) and on the incompleteness part of V7. Procrustes-type scores have no interpretable upper bound, so the study cannot show how much is lost in mapping, and V4 is not really tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the representations of the studied 7B LLMs do not seem universal, with some models substantially different. They also identify three challenges for measuring similarity: discrepancies between measures, task dependency, and difficulty of interpreting scores.
record.recipe_differences: Measures final-layer representations of released LLMs across model families and tasks using several similarity measures; it does not compare independently trained same-architecture seed runs or perform a model-scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity patterns differ across measures and datasets. The study uses a specific prompt format and notes that prompt choice may influence similarity, but does not experimentally vary prompts.
record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The datasets are limited in size, with fewer samples than representation dimensions; this may overestimate scores for alignment-based measures. Only models of a specific size are studied, so generalization to other sizes is unclear. A specific prompt format is used and prompt effects on representations are not studied in detail. Some reported scores lack an interpretable upper bound. The text does not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Individual pairwise heatmap cells in Figures 1 and 2 are not separately recorded: the supplied text gives plotted color patterns but no cell values, and the paper's prose summaries and aggregate correlations are recorded instead.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; all models are ~7B.
No reconstruction loss, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping. Procrustes scores are unbounded and uninterpretable as mapping quality.
Neighbour count fixed at k=10. No out-of-distribution inputs. Prompt format not varied.
No plateau test. No causal test of shared data or objectives. Absolute degree of alignment not interpretable.

missing.what: Results with OT+IS+TR invariance, adding RSA and CKA. Text says they are similar to Figure 1 and that patterns still differ between measures. Bears on whether the invariance choice changes conclusions.
missing.locator: Section 3.1 first paragraph; Appendix C, Figure 2

missing.what: Limitation: with fewer samples than dimensions, alignment-based measures (Procrustes, Aligned Cossim) may overfit and overestimate similarity. Aligned Cossim values are ~0.98–0.998.
Scores of Orthogonal Procrustes and Norm RSM-Diff lack an upper bound, so uniform scores could mean equally similar or equally dissimilar.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short NeurIPS workshop-style paper whose heatmaps have no numeric cell values. The V4 links were removed because Procrustes is used here as a similarity score with no interpretable bound, not as a mapping-loss test. The record's V4 limits_scope label is dropped. The V7 support rests on relative non-uniformity, not on an absolute alignment level.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or comparison of representational alignment with model capability; all studied models are roughly 7B parameters.
No paired image-caption inputs or vision-language model comparisons.
No comparison across random seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
The study evaluates representation alignment, including orthogonal Procrustes, but does not test functional interchangeability, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired inputs.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Tests two benchmark datasets and several similarity measures, but not different neighbour counts beyond the reported k=10 setting or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete/non-uniform similarity patterns, but does not test a plateau with scale or determine whether shared data or objectives cause alignment.

relationships.condition: Winogrande and cross-dataset comparisons, OT+IS invariance, 4 measures
relationships.reason: Falcon's dissimilarity depends on the measure (r1–r4). GPT-J and OPT stand out only under some measures (r5, r6). Measure heatmaps correlate at ρ=0.35 (r11). Patterns correlate across datasets at only ρ=0.34 (r13), and GPT-J flips between datasets (r14, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Falcon, GPT-J and OPT appeared distinctive under different measures, whose heatmaps correlated at only ρ=0.35; cross-dataset patterns correlated at ρ=0.34, with GPT-J changing its pattern between datasets.

relationships.reason: Measures agree substantially more on HumanEval (ρ=0.65, r12); Procrustes and Norm RSM-Diff show highly similar patterns there. Appendix results are similar when translation invariance is added (text, not rowed).
relationships.display_finding: Measure agreement increased to ρ=0.65, with Procrustes and Norm RSM-Diff showing highly similar patterns that remained similar after adding translation invariance.

relationships.condition: ~7B base LLMs of different families on Winogrande and HumanEval, relative comparisons only
relationships.reason: Several models (Falcon, StableLM Alpha, OpenLlama, OPT, CodeLlama-Python, GPT-J on code) are notably dissimilar to the rest. Authors conclude representations are not universal (r1, r2, r7–r10, r15). Absolute alignment level cannot be interpreted.
relationships.display_finding: Falcon, StableLM Alpha, OpenLlama, OPT, CodeLlama-Python and GPT-J on code were notably dissimilar to peers, though absolute alignment could not be interpreted.

tranche.reason: The study demonstrates metric and dataset dependence and argues against universal representations in the tested models, qualifying general convergence claims.

source_check.notes: The correlations measure agreement between heatmap patterns, not absolute model alignment. Appendix E warns that small datasets may inflate alignment-based scores; training-data explanations are expectations rather than controlled causal findings.
